block_labels.format: subject/session/task, where the official 'subject' column is re-indexed to '0' for this single-subject path
block_labels.trial_ids_per_block: 2-65 (64 production trials; trials 0-1 are the feedback training trials removed by official cleaning)

historical_block1_parity.differences: Only cosmetic string formatting from the pandas version that wrote each pickle: sentence_UID/button_unique_id render ids as '1' vs '1.0', and the Meg row gets a 'nan_' UID. No event content differs.
historical_block1_parity.handoff_2918_2119_666_132_figures: Those were the RAW pre-cleaning counts (events_raw.pkl: 2918 rows, 2119 keystrokes, 666 words, 132 sentences incl. 66 perceptual). The cleaned block1 has always been 2743/2040/638/64.

sentence_list_verification.hypothesis_from_filenames: list1 = session1 block1 + session2 block2; list2 = session1 block2 + session2 block1
sentence_list_verification.evidence: Jaccard 1.0 (64/64 shared) for both list pairs and 0.0 for all cross-list pairs.
sentence_list_verification.consequence: Every S22 sentence is typed exactly twice, once per session. Cross-session splits are NOT sentence-disjoint by default.
sentence_list_verification.supporting_signal: list2 blocks have visibly longer sentences and more keystrokes (2755/2792) than list1 blocks (2040/2063).

split_relevant_summary.within_block: 64 production trials per block (was 8 used in 5A-5V).
split_relevant_summary.cross_block_same_session: session1 block1 (list1) vs session1 block2 (list2): different sentences, same day.
split_relevant_summary.cross_session: session1 vs session2: different day; but list1/list2 reappear swapped, so sentence text repeats.
split_relevant_summary.sentence_disjoint: Requires grouping by sentence text: train on list1 blocks, evaluate on list2 blocks (or vice versa), which is simultaneously sentence-disjoint and block-disjoint.
split_relevant_summary.note: Split design itself is out of scope for 5X.

environment.note: events_clean_all_blocks.pkl is written by that env's pandas 2.2.3; the older events_clean.pkl was written by the newer workspace pandas and cannot be read back by the official env.
